hypothesis: Decoupling wind speed from direction via cyclic sin/cos encoding will improve low-wind directional representation, reducing T+1 wind errors and boundary overshoots.
evidence_anchor: Failure slice (e): low-wind direction is masked by magnitude in (wind_x, wind_y) normalized components; also ZSSS T+1 wind_x regression head micro-overflow (>1) indicates poor boundary fitting at low wind speeds.
expected_effect: Reduce T+1 RMSE by ~0.002-0.005 and eliminate >1 wind_x predictions on low-wind slices.
falsification: If T+1 RMSE on low_wind_slice does not improve by at least 0.001 (or any >1 wind_x prediction remains) across all three seeds, the trial is refuted.
patch_plan: In build_forecast_inputs, replace or augment the normalized (wind_x, wind_y) features with sin/cos of wind direction (from original u/v) and a separate wind speed feature. Keep original components optionally but ensure decoupling. For variant 'sincos_plus_speed_decouple', also add wind speed as an explicit channel. Update AllowedContextEncoder to handle the new feature dimensions without changing signatures.
